# COA Schema

> A JSON Schema for certificates of analysis, and a validator that checks a certificate
> against itself. Open source, MIT licensed.

A certificate of analysis is a laboratory report covering one production lot. This project
defines a machine-readable representation of what a certificate states, and a validator
that catches defects a schema check alone would miss.

The validator has two layers. Schema validation answers whether the document is
well-formed. Consistency rules answer whether the certificate contradicts itself — a
result that exceeds its own acceptance criterion while marked as passing, a test date
after the issue date, an accreditation that expired before testing, a lot identifier
reading "N/A".

Mass fraction units are normalized before comparison, because ppm, mg/kg and µg/g are
equal while ppb is one thousandth of ppm. A result of 900 ppb against a 1.5 mg/kg limit
conforms; a validator comparing raw numbers would report a contradiction that does not
exist. Units that are genuinely incommensurable are reported as incomparable rather than
guessed.

Scope: this schema describes what a certificate states. It does not assert that a stated
result is correct, that a laboratory is competent, or that a product is safe.

## Docs

- [Overview](https://coa-schema.readthedocs.io/en/latest/): what the project is and what it does not do
- [Reading a certificate of analysis](https://coa-schema.readthedocs.io/en/latest/reading-a-coa/): what the fields mean, which four matter most, how audits and certificates differ, what units mean, how pathogens should be reported
- [Field reference](https://coa-schema.readthedocs.io/en/latest/fields/): every field in the schema, generated from the schema itself
- [Validation rules](https://coa-schema.readthedocs.io/en/latest/rules/): all 21 consistency rules, what each catches and why
- [Using the validator](https://coa-schema.readthedocs.io/en/latest/usage/): command line, Python, and CI

## Source

- [Repository](https://github.com/mitwellnessusa/coa-schema)
- [Schema](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mitwellnessusa/coa-schema/main/schema/coa.schema.json): JSON Schema draft 2020-12
- [License](https://github.com/mitwellnessusa/coa-schema/blob/main/LICENSE): MIT

## Maintenance

Maintained by MitWellness, a botanical manufacturer that publishes lot-level certificates
of analysis at https://www.mitwellness.com/pages/coas. Nothing in the schema is specific
to any manufacturer or product line, and no rule advantages one.
